name: Newsletter Subscribe + New Release Notification | template

nodes.name: Newsletter Subscribe Webhook
nodes.notes: Your website/app calls POST https://<your-n8n>/webhook/newsletter-subscribe with body { "email": "..." }. Configure header auth if you want to protect the endpoint.

nodes.name: Check Existing Subscriber
nodes.notes: With Always Output Data enabled: if no row is found, the original item continues without an id field. If an existing row is found, that row continues with its id field.

nodes.name: Save New Subscriber
nodes.notes: If you add subscribed_at or active columns to the table later, also add them here in value.

parameters.jsCode:
const meta = $('Normalize Email').first().json; const html = `

Welcome to Your Product updates

Thanks for subscribing. You will receive concise emails when important product releases are published.

Before using this template, replace this copy with your product name, support links, unsubscribe language, and any legal footer your audience requires.

You are receiving this email because you subscribed to product updates.

`; return [{ json: { email: meta.email, subject: 'Welcome to Your Product updates', html } }];

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "success": true, "message": "You were already subscribed; no new email was sent" } }}

nodes.name: New Release Webhook
nodes.notes: Production webhook. Required JSON fields: version and SEND_EMAIL=YES. Optional: changelog. Empty/missing fields now fail before any subscriber email is sent.

nodes.name: Configure Manual Send
nodes.notes: Manual path: edit these plain text fields before pressing Execute. version accepts v7.15.1 v7.15.2 v7.15.3, 7.15.1 7.15.2 7.15.3, or comma-separated versions. Set SEND_EMAIL exactly to YES only when you really want to send to subscribers.

nodes.name: Read README from GitHub
nodes.notes: If the repository default branch is master instead of main, update the URL. Automatic retry is enabled for transient network errors.

nodes.name: Extract Requested Release Versions
nodes.notes: Parses requested versions, extracts changelog sections, groups real features into unique user-facing highlights, and filters technical noise before email generation.

options.systemMessage:
=You are the official copywriter for "Your Product", the product configured for this workflow.

ABSOLUTE LANGUAGE RULE:
- Write ONLY in English.
- Never use Italian words, Italian sentences, or Italian UI labels in the email content.
- If the changelog or developer note contains Italian, translate it to natural English before using it.

EDITORIAL RULES — ANTI AI-SLOP:
- The email must focus only on real, user-visible changes: new features, visible behavior changes, important bug fixes, privacy/permission changes, or documentation that materially changes what users understand.
- Do not make internal maintenance sound like a feature. Ignore version bumps, dependency updates, refactors, linting, CI, build chores, formatting, and generic docs polish unless they directly affect users.
- Use the Editorial brief as the main source and priority order. Use the raw changelog only to fact-check.
- If there are no meaningful user-visible changes, write honestly that this is a small maintenance update; do not invent benefits.

FORBIDDEN GENERIC PHRASES:
- Do not write: "latest improvements", "enhanced experience", "seamless", "powerful", "various fixes", "better performance", "improved reliability", "new version is available", "full changelog", or "complete release notes" unless immediately followed by a concrete sourced detail.
- Do not use marketing filler. Every highlight needs a specific changed thing and why it matters.

CONTEXT:
- You are writing the email subscribers receive when one or more versions are announced together.
- Current label: {{ $json.version_label || $json.version }}.
- If multiple versions are included, write one aggregated update, not separate mini-emails.

FACT-CHECKING RULES:
- Every sentence must be directly supported by the editorial brief, changelog, README context, or developer note.
- Do not add setup, pricing, paid-plan, unlimited sync, future guarantees, or convenience claims unless the source explicitly says them.
- Prefer precise, modest wording over marketing claims.

STYLE RULES:
- Tone: friendly, clear, and useful. Never corporate, never hype.
- Explain important changes from the user's point of view: what changed, why it matters, and whether the user needs to do anything.
- Maximum 5 highlights, ordered by user value across all included versions.
- Each highlight must be self-contained and specific.
- Do not mention reviews, welcome text, or subscription: this email is only for existing subscribers and only about the release update.

OUTPUT:
Return ONLY the requested structured schema (subject, intro, highlights, closing). No extra text outside the schema.

nodes.name: AI Agent - Copywriter Release
nodes.notes: If retries and parser auto-fix still do not produce valid output, the error is caught and the flow continues through the No AI fallback branch.

nodes.name: Structured Output Parser
nodes.notes: Auto-fix is enabled: if the model output does not match the schema, the node asks the model for one automatic JSON correction before throwing an error. If your n8n version does not keep the toggle enabled after import, enable Auto-Fix Format manually in the node parameters.

nodes.name: Release Email Fallback (No AI)
nodes.notes: Deterministic English-only fallback. Uses grouped changelog notes for single or multi-version release notifications and avoids generic placeholder copy.

nodes.name: Prepared Email Content
nodes.notes: Convergence point: receives output from either the successful AI branch or the fallback branch. Downstream nodes always read from this node, regardless of which branch produced the content.

nodes.name: Read Subscribers
nodes.notes: Empty filter = all rows. If you add an active column later, filter here with active=true to manage unsubscribes.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "success": true, "message": "Notification sent", "version": $('Extract Requested Release Versions').first().json.version_label, "versions": $('Extract Requested Release Versions').first().json.versions, "recipients": $('Read Subscribers').all().length, "quality_gate": $('Prepared Email Content').first().json.quality_gate } }}

parameters.content:
Release notification test area

Production path uses Data Table → Loop Subscribers → Send Release Email.
For single-recipient tests, duplicate the workflow or replace Read Subscribers with one temporary Code/Set item using test@example.com, then restore the Data Table node before production use.

nodes.name: Start Newsletter Send
nodes.notes: Manual production trigger. Edit "Configure Manual Send" first: version=<versions>, SEND_EMAIL=YES. Missing values fail before any email node.

nodes.name: Validate Newsletter Send
nodes.notes: Hard stop: version must contain at least one x.y.z version and SEND_EMAIL must be exactly YES. Otherwise the workflow errors before reading subscribers or sending emails.

nodes.name: Configure Webhook Send
nodes.notes: Webhook path: send JSON fields version, optional changelog, and SEND_EMAIL=YES. Empty or missing version, or missing SEND_EMAIL=YES, stops before any email node.
